articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Electromagnetic-Wave Absorber for IEEE 802.15.3d
abstract: A 300-GHz band is a promising frequency band for ultra-high-speed future wireless communication. To realize it, a method using an electromagnetic-wave (EM-wave) absorber has been desired to suppress the cavity resonance of a transceiver module and to increase reliability. In this paper, we show an ultra-wideband EM-wave absorber for IEEE Standard 802.15.3d.

articleTitle: Path Loss and Multipath Profiles in a Street Canyon based on 253 GHz Measurements
abstract: We measured 253 GHz sub-terahertz (THz) channel by a wideband channel sounder in a street canyon environment. The channel measurements were collected by rotating horn antennas for high power gain and angular resolution. Omnidirectional channel characteristics were analyzed by synthesizing the measurement data. The path loss, power-delay profile, and power-angular profile were computed from the synthesized data. The measurement results of path loss, delay spread, and angular spread according to the distance were provided in this paper.

articleTitle: A Review of the D-band Antennas
abstract: This paper presents a review of the D-band antennas. The antennas are designed using several technologies such as low temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCC), printed circuit board (PCB), on-chip, metallic waveguide, 3-D printing, etc. The survey shows that the linearly polarized (LP) antennas with broadside radiation characteristics have been extensively studied, while less data is available for circularly polarized (CP) antennas. Similarly, only a few designs of LP end-fire antennas have been presented, while only one dual-polarized antenna is present. The waveguide-PCB transitions are required for antenna measurements and have also been discussed.

articleTitle: A Ku-band Cascode Low Noise Amplifier using InGaAs E-mode 0.15-um pHEMT Technology
abstract: Low-power operation and ease of system integration are increasingly important in a system using multiple amplifiers in parallel, such as a phased array. In this paper, a Kuband pseudomorphic high electron mobility transister (pHEMT) low-noise amplifier (LNA) that can be applied to such a system was designed and measured. The chip was fabricated using InGaAs Enhanced-mode (E-mode) 0.15-um pHEMT process. And by applying a cascode configuration that reuses current to the circuit, it consumes low power and has high gain. The current consumption is 5mA at 4V supply voltage, and the gain is 21.3 dB at 16 GHz. The 3-dB bandwidth of the LNA is 2.59 GHz and noise Figure (NF) is 1.46 dB at 16 GHz. OP1dB is 8.05 dBm and IP1dB is -10.8 dBm. The size of the entire chip including the electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection pad is 1.5x0.95 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Integrated Frequency Synthesizer with an Improved LC-Tank Colpitts Voltage-Controlled Oscillator
abstract: A 5.6 GHz band frequency synthesizer with an improved LC-tank Colpitts voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) has been designed and successfully implemented in tsmc 0.18 $\mu$m CMOS technology. The VCO is formed by two complementary nMOS and pMOS transistors for generating negative resistance to compensate the loss in the LC-tank of the VCO. A 3-bit binary weighted capacitor array is connected to the LC-tank for frequency coarse tuning and a gain boosting Colpitts technique is employed to achieve low power consumption and reduce phase noise. Under the supply voltage of1.8 V, measured results introduce that the output frequency is tuneable from 5.25 to 5.75 GHz corresponding to 9.1% with a power consumption of 17.8 mW, the phase noise at 1 MHz offset frequency from 5.6 GHz is -110.12dBc/Hz and the output power spectrum at the locked frequency of 5.606 GHz is -3.14dBm. Including pads, the chip dimension is 0.665 $(0.774\times 0.86)\mathrm{m}\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

articleTitle: Near Field Measurement and Analysis of Millimeter Wave at 20GHz and 30GHz
abstract: Theoretical attenuation of RF in free space is characterized according to Friis equation which is based on far field range. This paper gives measurement results of space insertion loss of millimeter wave at 20GHz and 30GHz, which separating between transmitting and receiving antennas is changed from lmm to 1400mm with lmm step. Measuring includes all range with reactive, Fresnel and far field. New formula to calculate free space attenuation is introduced, to resolve discrepancy of theoretical and experimental values. It shows good agreement between their values in a part of reactive range and Fresnel range, of course, including far field range. Antenna measurement method in near field is also proposed in basis of the result.

articleTitle: Wideband Dual-Polarized On-Board Antenna for 5G mmWave Mobile Application
abstract: This paper describes a wideband dual-polarized antenna array for 5G mmWave mobile application. An air cavity structure is introduced to mitigate the high loss tangent of the FR4 substrate. Slot-coupled feeding and parasitic patches are used to improve the impedance bandwidth of the patch antenna. The measured bandwidth is 23.1 % (23 ~ 29 GHz). In virtue of wide bandwidth, high gain, and good spatial coverage, the proposed design strategy is promising for future 5G mmWave mobile phones.

articleTitle: A 39-GHz Up- and Down-Conversion Mixer System in 65-nm CMOS for 5G Communication
abstract: This paper presents a 39-GHz up- and downconversion mixer system in 65-nm CMOS for 5G mmWave communication. To achieve high conversion gain and low LO leakage, the active Gilbert cell is adopted for both upconversion and down-conversion mixer. To address high isolation and low insertion loss, a pi-type impedance matching network and a series-shunt structure are introduced for LO/RF and IF switches, respectively. In addition, capacitive neutralized differential IF and RF buffers are introduced to enhance the power gain and output linearity of the up- and down-conversion mixer, respectively. Fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS process, the up- and down-conversion mixer system realizes a measured conversion gain of 1± 1.5dB and 3.5± 1.5dB from 34.7 to 41.2 GHz and 32 to 42.3 GHz, respectively. At the maximum conversion gain, the up-conversion mixer achieves an output 1-dB gain compression point (OPldB) 2.5 dBm. From 34 to 41.5 GHz, the down-conversion mixer achieves a third-order output intercept point (OIP3) from 8.4 to 9dBm.

articleTitle: Sub-THz III-V on Si technologies for 6G electronics
abstract: In this work, we will highlight the need for a mature and upscaled III-V technology to address the needs for the power amplifiers in next generation 6G applications, where the vision is to move to operating frequencies above 100GHz. III-V upscaling ultimately allows to enable a hybrid III-V/CMOS technology to reduce power consumption but also enable a much smaller footprint. We will also discuss the possible co-integration schemes to combine these devices with standard CMOS, used for the beamforming, and how to connect to the antennas.

articleTitle: 120-GHz On-Chip Folded Dipole Antenna With Integrated Artificial Magnetic Conductor Structures
abstract: A 120-GHz folded dipole antenna including artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) structures is proposed to improve antenna gain and reduce the radiation pattern size on the standard 65-nm CMOS process. The proposed AMC structures designed in a square cushion array are constructed between the ground plane and the radiation pattern of the antenna for minimizing the signal leakage to a Si substrate. The physical size of the proposed antenna is reduced by the proposed AMC structures which change the substrate characteristics at the resonant frequency of the AMC. The ground plane of the antenna is located at the bottom of the substrate with a thickness of300 $\mu \mathrm{m}$, and the radiation patterns (a) and AMC structures of the antenna are designed in the highest metal layer (M9) and the lowest metal layer (M1) of the 65-nm CMOS process, respectively. At a center frequency of120-GHz, the proposed antenna including an $11\times 5$ AMC array showed an antenna gain of1.6 $\mathrm{d}\mathrm{B}\mathrm{i}$, a radiation efficiency of 51%, a 10- dB bandwidth of 10.1 GHz, and a vertical/horizontal 3-dB beamwidth of 147°/113° in the simulation results using ANSYS HFSS. The proposed antenna exhibited a size reduction of 26% compared to the conventional antenna.

articleTitle: Millimetre-Wave Direct Detection Receivers for Earth Observation Instruments – Trends and Challenges
abstract: Advances in semiconductor technologies and integration techniques have paved way for continuous performance improvements in passive mm-wave instruments and sensors. Extending the operating frequencies towards the THz region and improvements of noise Figure and 1/f noise performance have become possible through continuous developments in very short gate-length low-noise metamorphic GaAs and InP MMIC processes and in Schottky detector technologies. While these technologies are the keys for heterodyne radiometers, they are in fact enablers for direct detection (DD) receivers. Concept of direct detection is one of the current trends which is dependent on developments in mmwave and sub-mm wave LNA technologies, zero-bias Schottky detector devices and RF channel filters. These blocks shall offer adequate sensitivity, low power consumption and minimum volume tojustify the development and inclusion of the receivers in focal arrays and in small satellites. In this paper, we will refer to the latest achievements and justify the future development plans and specifications of direct detection radiometer developments for future ESA missions.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement Method of Small Cassegrain Antenna for Long-Distance Transmission
abstract: A sub-THz Cassegrain antenna for long-distance transmission was designed, manufactured, and measured. We designed the main reflector to have a diameter of 30 mm to obtain a gain of 30 dBi or more and a relatively wider beam width than a general Cassegrain antenna. The proposed antenna has a gain of 36.8 dBi and a beam width of 2.5° at 245 GHz. The received power level and radiation pattern were measured by configuring a measurement environment to measure the performance of the sub-THz antenna. The commercial horn antenna and the proposed Cassegrain antenna were compared and measured. The transmitter consists of an analog signal generator (ASG) and an up-converter (UC), and a commercial horn antenna with 24 dBi gain at 245 GHz is attached to the upconverter. The receiver consists of a signal analyzer (SA) and a down-converter (DC), and the proposed Cassegrain antenna is attached to the down-converter. We compared the measured and simulated results to obtain reliable measurement results without using an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: A 24-30GHz Wideband Power Amplifier With High-Coupling-Coefficient Transmission Line Transformer and Staggered Tuning
abstract: In this paper, a 24-30GHz wideband power amplifier for millimeter-wave 5G communication is presented. Wideband small-signal matching is achieved with a staggered tuning technique. The input of the driver stage is matched at 30 GHz and the input of the power stage is matched at 24 GHz. A high-coupling-coefficient transmission line transformer (TLT) matching network is used for wideband output impedance matching. It compensates the large-signal device output capacitance for the operating frequency. To improve linearity, active feedback linearizer (AFL) and 2nd harmonic termination techniques are used. At the operating frequency, it achieves 19.8-21.7 dB peak gain, 15.6-17.7 dBm OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> 17.4-19.3 dBm P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>, and 20.4-31.4% PAE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">peak</inf>. The 3-dB bandwidth is 23.2-31.0 GHz, and the core size is 0.134 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Broadband CMOS Doherty Power Amplifier with Asymmetric-Transformer-based Output Matching Network
abstract: This paper presents a 60-GHz Doherty power amplifier with asymmetric-transformer-based output matching network in 65-nm CMOS process. To achieve a high output-power-transfer efficiency with a high reliability, the proposed Doherty output matching network is implemented with fully-EM simulated transformer with a high-Q custom capacitor. The output matching parameters of the main and auxiliary PA are asymmetrically tuned to simultaneously match the optimum load-impedance at a high power. As a result, the PA achieves a peak gain of 12.7 dB and a 3-dB bandwidth of 55 to 69 GHz. The PA also achieves a peak P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> of 16.3 dBm, a peak PAE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ldB</inf> of 19.6 % and a peak PAE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6-dBOBO</inf> of 8 % in the overall frequency band. The PA is implemented with a compact size area of 0.21 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the dc quiescent power consumption is only 104.4 mW.

articleTitle: Series-Fed Printed Dipole Array Incorporated with Linear to Circular Polarization Metasurface Converter
abstract: In this paper, the design of a series-fed angled dipole array antenna incorporated with a polarization conversion metasurface is presented. The antenna consists of a two-layer cascaded metasurface made of 4×4 circular patches with cross-slots of unequal lengths placed above the series-fed angled dipole array antenna in the end-fire direction with an air gap. The series-fed angled dipole array antenna consists of eight dipole elements with equal spacing, and each dipole was connected to a parallel stripline printed on the front and backsides of the substrate. The metasurface made of a circular patch with cross-slots of unequal lengths is used for polarization conversion of the linearly polarized wave to the circularly polarized wave. The measured reflection coefficient for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < -10 dB results yield an impedance bandwidth of 26.2 to 31.4 GHz (18.0%), a 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 26.5 to 31.2 GHz (16.3%), a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 26.2--30.5 GHz (15.16%) with a peak gain of 10.9 dBic, and radiation efficiency of more than 80% within the AR bandwidth.

articleTitle: A 45-nm RFSOI CMOS Based Band-Reconfigurable Quadrature Hybrid for mm-Wave 5G Applications
abstract: We present a band-reconfigurable quadrature hybrid (QH) for in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) signal generation in a broadband Doherty power amplifier (PA) for millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) 5G application in a 45-nm RFSOI CMOS device technology. The band-reconfigurable QH has been implemented using a single transistor-based switch (SW) and its simulation results show an I/Q signal magnitude imbalance of less than 0.7 dB, and an I/Q signal phase imbalance of 88.7 – 90.5° in 5G NR bands (n258, n257). The core area of the band-reconfigurable QH is 230 µm × 110µm excluding the probing pads and input/output baluns for probing test.

articleTitle: Design of Aperture Coupled Ka-Band Phased Array Antenna Using Cavity PCB Process
abstract: This paper presents a design of the Ka-band 4x4 phased array antenna. The proposed antenna includes four beamforming ICs, and space for embedding the beamforming IC in the printed circuit board (PCB) is secured through the cavity process. As the beamforming IC is embedded in the PCB, the height of the surface of the beamforming IC and the PCB surface becomes the same, so that the length of wire bonding is shortened. Therefore, the loss generated when the beamforming IC and the antenna are connected is reduced. The antenna is implemented and its performance is verified through measurement.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of GaN/Si versus GaAs LNAs in 5G mm-wave frontend context
abstract: This paper presents a comparative performance analysis of LNAs realized in GaAs and GaN/Si technologies in the context of 5G mmWave massive MIMO transceiver. Regardless the choice of architecture for beamforming, a key component of the base station transmitter is the RF frontend. In this paper, we investigate the linear and nonlinear performance in a gain/noise/linearity trade-off for the LNA. The circuits are fabricated using OMMIC technologies and characterized on board over the 24-30 GHz frequency band. Measurements demonstrate that it is interesting to use a GaN in a frontend thanks to its additional advantages in terms of linearity.

articleTitle: Flexible RF substrate and interconnection technology for > 100 GHz applications
abstract: We present a novel flexible RF substrate and interconnection technologies for > 100 GHz applications. In this contribution, the author will address flexible substrate technology for RF applications at the Fraunhofer Heinrich-Hertz Institute and present measurement results for test coupons. A 3 mm flexline is flip-chip bonded onto Si substrate and measured. 3 dB frequency of about 70 GHz was obtained and material parameters model for EM simulation was investigated.

articleTitle: A 60-GHz X-type Variable Gain Attenuator
abstract: A 60-GHz X-type attenuator with complementary bias control is proposed in this study. The proposed circuit was implemented with a 65-nm CMOS process and it occupies $520 \mu \mathrm{m}$ $\times 471 \mu \mathrm{m}$ including bonding pads. The measured peak gain is -6 dB, and 3 -dB bandwidth is over 18.2 GHz from 48.8 to over 67 GHz. In addition, proposed phase invertible attenuator achieves a gain control range of over $37 \mathrm{~dB}$ with maximum 14° phase variation in $60-\mathrm{GHz}$ band.

articleTitle: A 45-nm RFSOI CMOS Based Compact Doherty Power Amplifier For mm-wave 5G Applications
abstract: A compact Doherty power amplifier (PA) with a single transformer is demonstrated in a 45-nm RFSOI CMOS device technology. The newly designed 45-nm RFSOI based two-stage differential Doherty PA shows a saturated output power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SAT</inf>) of >21.2dBm, power gain of >18.8dB, and a peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of >34.3%at the 27 GHz CW signal. These results show much improved performances compared to our previous PA (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SAT</inf>: 18.8 dBm, peak PAE 30 %), which is fabricated in a 2S-nm bulk CMOS. Under the 5G NR 64 AM OF DM (PAPR >10dB), the PA IC exhibits superior linear output power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LIN</inf>) of 14.8 dBm and average PAE of 19.8 %. (a) The PA IC occupies as compact core area as 680 μm×280μm.

articleTitle: Antenna Front-end Technologies Featuring Antenna-on-Display and Antenna-in-Package to Enable 360° Beamforming Coverage for Millimeter-wave Wireless Connectivity
abstract: Phased array antenna technology has been imperative to ensure the wireless connectivity of millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless devices such as CPEs and cellular devices. Due to advances in CMOS technology, a typical 5G mmWave TRX can achieve a high output power of 10-15 dBm and minimum reference signal receive power (RSRP) of approximately -140 dBm [1]. However, the path to realizing the full potential of the millimeter wave technology is hindered by numerous technical challenges including size, cost, and power constraints. The research and development (R&D) group at KREEEMO Inc. has been focusing on integrating antennas and RF front-ends which can energy-efficiently improve mmWave beamforming coverage in indoor and outdoor scenarios. The speaker will discuss (1) current research and development on antenna packaging technology, (2) the hybrid antenna-on-display (AoD) and antenna-in-package (AiP) beamforming architecture featuring 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> beamforming coverage in a cellular device, and (3) the AiP design with stackable patch antenna (SPA) technology.

articleTitle: Development of Higher Order Rotating-mode Generator using Dielectric Rod Waveguide at Wband
abstract: We propose a novel method to generate a higher order rotating-mode by using of a dielectric rod waveguide (DRW) without quasi-optical (QO) mirror. Unlike a quasioptical mode generator, the DRW mode generator is relatively simple to align. We present the simulation and experiment results of the DRW mode generating system, and analysis for alignment issue.

articleTitle: Investigation of Beam Scanning Characteristics for 29.5 GHz Metamaterials Leaky-wave Antenna Using Variable Capacitance
abstract: leaky-wave antenna capable of beam steering using variable capacitance is designed at 29.5 GHz. The proposed beamforming metamaterial leaky wave antenna can be realized with variable capacitance controlled by DC bias voltage. While the beam is scanned, the impedance of the line is stably maintained the same. The length of the the designed 16-cell metamaterial leaky wave antenna is 2. 6mm x 32.1mm (0.26$\lambda_{0}$x3.16$\lambda_{0}$). It is shown to have the beam scanning range of 120° from 30° to 150° with a relatively small gain change between 10.6 dB and 12.9.

articleTitle: Vanadium Dioxide based Multifunctional Tunable Terahertz Filter using Metasurface
abstract: A multifunctional terahertz filter based on vanadium dioxide is realized. It can be electrically reconfigurable and features two different types of tunable frequency selective response depending on two orthogonal polarized incident fields. The mutually polarized response of the filter plays an important role in achieving active polarization angle control of transmitted fields.

articleTitle: Liquid-Metal, Flexible-Ceramic-Based Antenna for Extreme High-Temperature Conformal Seeker Applications
abstract: High-performance hypersonic vehicles such as airplanes and rockets require electronics such as RF seekers that can operate in temperatures over 50°C. A major limitation for high-frequency electronics operating in extreme temperatures is that metals and dielectrics melt or have degraded material properties that are critical for the intended application. Here we demonstrate a high-frequency antenna using a nontoxic gallium alloy liquid as a conductor and a high-temperature resin matrix as a dielectric; these materials can operate at temperatures over 1000°C for extended periods. The liquid metal has high thermal stability and can maintain its liquidity up to 1300°C. The dielectric has an inhibited elastic stage and a more fully reactive ceramic stage, which allows conformal device fabrication in coordination with the fluidic conductor. The dielectric spectra of the uncured, semi-cured, and cured ceramics were measured from 50 MHz to 20 GHz. A liquid-metal ground meandered antenna that uses the ceramic as a substrate was prototyped and operated at 550°C for 30 minutes with no significant performance degradation. This antenna can be used in high-temperature environments such those experienced by RF seekers.

articleTitle: Delay Spread Model for Super Proximity Environments at 285 GHz Band
abstract: ITU-R reported technical and operational characteristics of land-mobile service applications in the frequency range 275-450 GHz and one of services is a super proximity communication in-equipment. This paper proposes a delay spread model at 285 GHz band wireless communication for super proximity environments, between chips in a desktop-sized metal box. It models the delay properties due to many multiple reflections present inside the metal box. The measurement of delay spread characteristics were made at center frequency of 285 GHz and bandwidth of 20 GHz using a vector network analyzer, and horn antennas with a beam width of 60°. The two metal boxes, having different sizes each other were used as equipment environments. The distances between transmitter to receiver antenna were from 28 mm to 375 mm, and they were located with face-to-face or 90° bend. All cases were kept line-of-sight. The rms delay spread was got by measurement campaign, it was maximum 5.11 ns, minimum 0.19 ns, average 2.25 ns, and standard deviation 1.34 ns. It was represented as a simple equation with a function of path distance by multiple reflection

articleTitle: Improving Linearity of 28-GHz Two-Stage Power Amplifier in 28-nm FD-SOI CMOS Using Back-Gate Bias Control
abstract: This paper presents a highly linear 28-GHz power amplifier (PA) with an adaptive back-gate bias control for improving IMD3 and AM-AM distortion simultaneously. Thanks to the thin buried oxide in the fully-depleted silicon-oninsulator, back-gate bias allows controlling the threshold voltage of the transistors. In order to increase the linearity of PA, each back-gate bias of driver-stage and power-stage are controlled adaptively according to the input power. The twostage common source PA was fabricated in 2S-nm FD-SOI CMOS. At 2S GHz, the PA provides PSAT and PAE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MAX</inf> of 14.5 dBm and 23.0%, respectively. With the adaptive back-gate bias control, IMD3 at 6 dB back-off output power is improved by around 12 dB, resulting in IMD3 <-37dBc at 28 GHz. Meanwhile, peak AM-AM distortion remained at <0.5dB.

Index Terms: 28-nm Fully Depleted Silicon On Insulator CMOS

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Retrodirective Beamformer Based on Waveguide Rotman Lens
abstract: In this paper, a mmWave based wireless power transfer (WPT) System at Ka-band is proposed for powering small devices at range. The proposed WPT System utilizes the Rotman lens to achieve retrodirectivity, which is essential for selective beaming of wireless power to the device of interest. To this end, a waveguide high-gain Rotman lens beamformer combined with an array of horn antennas is designed. The beamformer consists of nine beam ports and exhibits a beam-steering coverage over a range of ±20° in 9 discrete directions with the gain of up to 26 dB.

articleTitle: OAM-mode modulator for millimeter wavelength range based on the ferroelectric lens
abstract: The design of the millimeter-wave OAM-mode modulator was proposed and analyzed. The proposed OAMmode modulator is based on the electrically controllable ferroelectric lens. The ferroelectric ceramic based on a solid solution of $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{a}_{x}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{r}{}_{1-x}\mathrm{T}\mathrm{i}\mathrm{O}_{3}$ was considered as a nonlinear material; however, the proposed design is not limited by this material. Such a lens has the advantages of compact dimensions, small response time, and negligible low current in a control circuit. It was shown in this work that the concentric ring topology of the radiotransparent electrodes can provide multiple OAM mode formations by a single ferroelectric modulator. The relationship between mode purity and ring topology dimensions for the proposed modulator design was investigated. A numerical simulation of multiple OAM mode formation by the proposed modulator was performed. The proposed device can be used for modulation and/or coding information due to OAM states transferred by a single carrier millimeter wave.

articleTitle: TRL-calibration Standards with Emphasis on Crosstalk Reduction
abstract: We present an innovative “shifted RF Pad” TRL on–wafer calibration kit to minimize the impact of crosstalk. The impact of the crosstalk in on-wafer measurement up to 330 GHz is observable by comparing results of DUTs obtained using the shifted and conventional RF pad calibration kit during calibration. Use of shifted RF pad structures shows improvement in measured DUT characteristics owing to reduced crosstalk. In addition, simulation results obtained using EM simulator, TCAD and SPICE models are employed to analyze the on-wafer measurement of DUTs.

articleTitle: A Compact, Low Loss, and Broadband Two-Section Lumped-Element Wilkinson Power Combiner Using 130 nm SiGe HBT BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents a compact, low loss two-section lumped-element Wilkinson power combiner (WPC) supporting a decade bandwidth of2-20 GHz. Each λ/4 impedance transformer, necessary for implementing the WPC, is realized by four cascaded C-L-C $\pi$-networks that is embedded into a single 3-turn symmetric inductor. It achieves compact size, high passive efficiency, and high L-C cut-off frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) simultaneously. The design procedure of the λ/4 impedance transformer is described in detail. The prototype WPC was fabricated in 130 nm SiGe HBT BiCMOS technology, with an active area of 0.34 × 0.36mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed two-section lumped element WPC attained the minimum insertion loss of 0.65 dB and its passive efficiency remains higher than 63% at 20 GHz. Return losses and isolation are higher than 10.0 and 7.0 dB, respectively, from 2 to 20 GHz.

articleTitle: Simulation of Electron Beams with Nonuniform Particle Density for Traveling-Wave Tubes in Emittance-Dominated Regime
abstract: In the millimeter wave and terahertz regime, inclusion of beam emittance while designing a traveling-wave tube (TWT) is important as the effects of beam emittance dominates those of space charge. The beam emittance affects performance of the TWT as well as transport of the electron beam. In particular, the equilibrium particle distribution is not uniform in the emittance-dominated regime. To simulate transport of electron beams having the nonuniform particle density, the stationary beam distributions in constant magnetic field such as Kapchinsky-Vladimirsky (K-V), waterbag, and Gaussian, are used. The numerical simulations are conducted using a CST Studio Suite by importing the generated distributions into the simulations. The results show that the transport of stationary beam distributions is stable.

articleTitle: CMOS Based Sub-THz Wireless Transceivers: Issues and Solutions
abstract: This talk will summarize the state-of-the-art sub-THz radio transceiver technologies focusing on CMOS technology, and identify the limiting factors and issues in terms of architectures and circuit topologies. Then, present the approaches and solutions that have been proposed by the members of the speaker’s team at KAIST

articleTitle: Beam-Reconfigurable Terahertz Metasurface with Optical Activations
abstract: Ultrafast reconfigurable devices with high-speed responses, high-resolution capabilities and ultra-compact sizes play important role in the real-time terahertz imaging, nondestructive detection, and low-latency communication systems. Reconfigurable terahertz metasurfaces as one of the reconfigurable devices, have enabled conspicuous functionalities of subwavelength planar devices and components for manipulating electromagnetic (EM) waves thanks to the ability at active and programmable controls. In this work, a coding metasurface integrating patterned phase change materials (PCMs), GeTe, is proposed. The proposed design benefits from the functionalities through different coding patterns and is capable of controlling beam tilting, directivity, and splitting of terahertz beams. The proposed concept was validated by feeding a metasurface with a wideband antenna while it can direct the main beam to 0 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> and 40 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> radiation with side lobe level of -15 dB.

articleTitle: Rediscovery of Glass Materials for Millimeter-wave Wireless Communications
abstract: Over the past 30 years, as mobile communication evolved from 1G to 4G, associated technologies have become increasingly sophisticated. But the 5G era still needs more innovative solutions to meet higher level specifications. Glass materials have received a lot of attention in recent years because they have many advantages in fabricating sensitive 5G components. This paper compares various properties, between glass and incumbent materials, such as, surface roughness, fine patterning and vias, Young’s modulus, etc. Additionally, various types of Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) are introduced in this paper because FSS is a basic technology for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) applied to 5G and 6G communications. Furthermore, 6G will use higher frequency bands than 5G, so it is expected that high quality material like glass will be increasingly required.

articleTitle: Beamforming Synthesis for Initial Access Fairness in Wireless Networks
abstract: This article introduces an Initial Access Fairness Beamforming (IAFB) approach for wireless networks using millimeter wave and terahertz frequencies and proposes novel synthesis method. The fairness is establishing independence between user location and the initial access signals received power level. We propose codeword synthesis with phase-only control which is beneficial for passive implementation of the receiver (Rx) and improves power utilization at the transmitter (Tx), which reduces mutual coupling impact for both Rx and Tx directions. In contrast to classical shaped beam synthesis methods where desired radiation patterns are targeted, we target the fairness of the received power distribution at the desired coverage area by solving a multi-objective nonconvex optimization problem. We address the known nonconvex optimization issues of initial state sensitivity and convergence rate by splitting the problem into a sequence of concatenated sub-problems, where the solution of one sub-problem defines the initial state for the next sub-problem.

articleTitle: Widely Tunable CMOS Voltage-Controlled Oscillator in K-Band
abstract: A CMOS LC voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) using a 3-bit switched-capacitor bank is proposed for improving frequency bandwidth in K-band. The capacitor bank is composed of metal-oxide-metal capacitors (MoM), which have low parasitic resistances, instead of the metal-insulator-metal capacitors to increase a quality factor of an LC tank. The proposed K-band VCO improves the phase noise characteristics in a wide frequency range by optimizing the unit size of both MoM and MOS varactor capacitors and the LC tank design based on full-EM simulation considering the interconnection characteristics in the cross-coupled oscillation core. The size of the proposed VCO was 400 $\mu \mathrm{m}\times 610\mu \mathrm{m}$, implemented on the TSMC 65-nm RFCMOS process. The overall tuning range of the proposed VCO was measured from IS.S2 to 23. 2S GHz at the output of a common-source buffer. The measured output power was -1.35dBm at a 1-V supply voltage with a power consumption of 46.4 mW at 21.45 GHz. The phase noise was measured to -105.8dBc/Hz at a 1-MHz frequency offset. A figure-of-merit (FOM) and a FOM incorporating the tuning range (FOM$\tau$) were calculated to -179dBc/Hz and -185.2dBc/Hz at the frequency offset, respectively.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective and Compact Antenna Applications Using Planar HIS: Research Survey and Possibility
abstract: This paper presents cost-effective and compact antenna applications at microwave and millimeter-wave (mmWave) spectrum using planar high-impedance surfaces (HIS). First, as an antenna element in this paper, a compact inverted-L antenna (ILA) operating at microwave spectrum has been presented using with one-dimensional electromagnetic bandgap (1-D EBG) ground structures fabricated on FR-4 PCB. The 1-D EBG ground structures of ILA within a compact size (0.21λ <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ×0.32 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> can serve as HIS with slow-wave behavior. The proposed antenna topology exhibits high end-fire gain in broadband, despite absence of auxiliary circuits. Second, the compressed mm-Wave phased array fabricated on single-layer FR-4 PCB has been presented by incorporating the antenna topology and via wall structures as HIS characteristics. The phased array antenna consists of low-coupled radiating element in linear array configuration with 0.39λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> inter-element spacing. Finally, a mmWave mobile device prototype equipped with two sets of the 8element phased arrays is realized and characterized using the proposed antenna topology and low-loss grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) feeding networks with via fences.

articleTitle: 300GHz-Band CMOS Bi-Directional Transceiver for 6G Phased-Array Applications
abstract: The wide available bandwidth at the 300GHzband makes it one of the expected target bands of the 6G wireless systems as extremely high data rates will be in demand in the next decade. In this presentation, a 300GHz-band bidirectional transceiver implemented using 65nm CMOS will be introduced. The talk also includes the discussion about phasedarray implementation using the introduced transceiver.
